四级核心词汇 · 06英文原文

The Meter That Counted Air

把空气也算进去的水表 · 599 词 · 8 段 · 首次出现的目标词加粗

1The laundry paid for each cubic meter of water it consumed. After it automated the billing process and installed a new meter, the bill rose by a third. Yet the operator, Leon, had washed the same quantity of clothes. A supplier blamed excessive consumption. Leon suspected a defect. He asked an apprentice to analyze the data before anyone replaced the equipment.

2Ana read the manual and drew the layout. A wheel turned as fluid moved through a transparent tube. A magnetic component transmitted a signal to a circuit. A formula converted turns to liquid volume on a proportional scale. The transmission was reliable. The ratio was valid only while the tube held liquid alone. After a shift it could drain, then draw in air. Ana saw a bubble float past the wheel as she switched on the pump.

3A technician challenged her single observation. Ana constructed a simple model with a steel basin and a scale. She measured the mass of the water and calculated its equivalent volume. On a parallel line she let air enter the tube. The readings diverged, as Ana had predicted. The wheel was sensitive to the air as well as the water. That characteristic was the crucial factor the supplier had overlooked.

4The supplier suggested a sophisticated software application. Ana devised a compact mechanical solution. A vertical chamber could release air before it reached the wheel. She consulted a specialist about the dimensions and pressure. The chamber had to be able to withstand a surge. A flexible joint would make it compatible with the existing hardware. She chose a durable metal and left enough space to remove the chamber for maintenance. Ana obtained a capacity chart from the manufacturer. An external pipe could raise the pressure and exert force on the chamber's base. She recorded the input and the internal pressure during the first operation. Those numbers would help someone adapt the design to another machine.

5After they assembled it, a sensor sent an irregular signal. Ana followed a cable and saw moisture had penetrated a connector. She isolated the circuit, replaced the faulty element, and repeated the sequence. The device now detected a continuous flow. Its measurement corresponded to the water they collected. She saved the data in a database so another technician could reproduce the result without her help.

6The cooperative also wanted to cut energy use. Its boiler burned gas and emitted carbon dioxide. An engineer proposed harnessing heat from its exhaust. A trial could show whether that innovation would reduce emissions. Ana asked for a thorough baseline test first. If they modified two variables at once, they could not determine which improvement was effective. A separate experimental test could generate sufficient evidence.

7When the supplier came back, he proposed a patent. Ana asked him to revise the instruction sheet first. He had used an abstract diagram to explain a simple physical principle. She added an arrow to indicate where an air pocket formed. She then asked a trainee to follow its logic. He opened the correct valve in an instant. The straightforward test did more to improve the manual than a long debate about its wording.

8The cooperative corrected the bill and adopted a criterion for operational checks. If the meter and scale showed a significant gap, the operator should check the chamber first. When a manager asked how Ana had made the system efficient, she showed him the clear tube. Its value was that the phenomenon was virtually impossible to miss. The team had refined its method by paying attention to something they had once dismissed as a bubble.

四级核心词汇 · 06中文译文

把空气也算进去的水表

按英文段落顺序对照阅读

1洗衣房按用掉的水量付费，每立方米都算钱。收费流程改成自动计算、又装上新表后，账单涨了三分之一。可操作员莱昂洗的衣服数量没变。供货商说是用水过量，莱昂却怀疑设备有缺陷。他请一名学徒先分析数据，查清楚了再决定是否更换设备。

2安娜读完说明书，画出装置布局。液体流经一根透明管时，会带动里面的轮子。一个磁性部件把信号传给电路，公式再按比例把转动次数换算成液体体积。信号传输没有问题。只有当管里全是液体时，那个比例才有效。下班后，管道可能把水排光，接着吸进空气。安娜打开泵，看到一个气泡漂过小轮。

3一名技术员质疑，只看一次能说明什么。安娜就用钢盆和秤搭了一个简易模型。她称出水的质量，算出相应的体积，再从一条并行的管路把空气引入管子。正如她预计的，两种测量的读数分开了。小轮遇到空气也会转，这正是供货商漏掉的关键。

4供货商建议用一套复杂的软件，安娜则想出一个小巧的机械方案。竖直装一个小腔室，就能在空气碰到轮子前把它放掉。她向行家请教尺寸和压力。腔室得扛得住突然增大的压力，接一个柔性接头就能与现有设备配合。她选了结实的金属，也留了拆卸检修的空间。安娜向制造商要来容量表。外接管可能提高压力，把力加到腔室底部。第一次运行时，她记下输入量和内部压力。以后有人要把设计用在另一台机器上，这些数字也能派上用场。

5装好后，一只传感器的信号忽稳忽乱。安娜顺着电缆查，发现水汽渗进了一个接头。她隔离电路，更换故障零件，然后按同样的顺序再做一遍。现在装置能测出连续水流，测得的量也与实际收集的水对得上。她把数据存进数据库，这样另一名技术员也能独立复现结果。

6合作社还想降低能耗。锅炉烧燃气，会排出二氧化碳。一位工程师提议利用废气里的热量。试验可以检验这个改进能不能减少排放。安娜先要求做一次完整的基准测试。如果同时改动两个变量，大家就分不清是哪项改进起了作用。单独做一次试验才能给出足够的证据。

7供货商回来后提议申请专利，安娜请他先改说明页。他原来的示意图很抽象，讲的却是个简单的物理原理。安娜加上一个箭头，标出哪里会积出一团空气，然后请一个新学员顺着图理解。他马上打开了正确的阀门。这个直截了当的测试，比争论半天该怎么用词更能改好说明书。

8合作社改正了账单，也定了一条运行检查标准。如果水表和秤给出的结果差得明显，操作员就先查小腔室。经理问安娜怎样让系统变得更高效，安娜给他看那根透明管。现象摆在那里，几乎谁都能看见。团队改进方法，正是从认真看待一个曾被当成小事的气泡开始的。
